name: Anthony Chabot Campground
coord_source: ReserveAmerica's Anthony Chabot Regional Park overview page, read 2026-09-16. PARK PRECISION: the pair is on the park overview, and this park holds eight campgrounds -- the family campground and seven group camps scattered across it. The point answers 'how far is this park from home'; it does not navigate to a pitch.
reservation_method: Park office (not reservations): (510) 690-6676, or 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4502
nightly_entry_cutoff: 10:00 PM, and it is a lock-out rather than a courtesy: entry gates are locked every night at 10pm and NO entry is possible until they re-open at 8am the next morning. Campers may EXIT at any time, so a late departure is fine and a late arrival is not. Stated by EBRPD, unlike Del Valle's cutoff, which this project holds only as a visitor's near-miss report.
fee_notes: Per night: tent or RV site with no hook-ups $35; RV site with water, sewer and 30-amp electrical $45; tent only, hike-in $25. RESERVATION FEE $8 PER SITE on top of the nightly rate. RV sewage disposal $20/use. Limited overflow parking $8/night/vehicle. Firewood $10/bundle and charcoal $15/bag at the campground kiosk -- but there is NO CAMP STORE, so bring everything else. Accepts cash, Visa, MasterCard and Discover. Fees subject to change.
notes: THE SITE COUNT RESOLVES, AND THE PAGE'S OWN LIST IS WRONG. 12 RV + 53 drive-up tent + 10 hike-in is exactly 75, so the '1 developed group site' the prose lists inside those 75 does not belong there: Puma Point is real, but it is a separate unit, not one of the 75 individual campsites. An earlier note here recorded the list as summing to 76 while calling itself 75; this is why. BEWARE A COINCIDENCE: the booking system's 'ALL 76' is NOT that same 76. It counts 69 individually listed sites plus 7 group camps, while the prose's faulty list counts 75 individual sites plus Puma Point. Two different quantities that happen to match. ONLY 69 OF THE 75 INDIVIDUAL SITES APPEAR ONLINE. Sites 010, 031, 033, 039, 053 and 075 are absent from the booking system's list entirely, so browsing online does not show the full inventory and a party counting availability there is counting 69. WHY THEY ARE ABSENT IS NOT STATED. The likeliest reading is that they are the accessible sites -- the same booking system says ADA campsites must be reserved by phone only, and the brochure confirms disabled accessible sites exist here -- but no source read says so, and they could equally be closed or out of service. Treated as a hypothesis, not a fact; ask Reservations. LOOPS, which the booking system names and no other source does: Loop A sites 1-12, the RV sites with 30-amp full hookups (11 listed, 010 absent); Loop B sites 13-22, 'Hike-In Sites (NO driving to site)', all 10 listed; Loop C sites 23-33, tent, 9 listed; Loop D sites 34-61, tent, 26 listed; Loop F sites 62-75, tent, 13 listed. There is no Loop E. PETS ARE ALLOWED AT EVERY SITE without exception -- all 76 listings, group camps and hike-in sites included, carry the Pets Allowed marker. THE OPEN SEASON IS UNCONFIRMED AND IT IS THE FACT MOST LIKELY TO COST A TRIP. The booking system says SEASONALLY CLOSED 1 NOVEMBER - 1 APRIL, with select sites closed through May. THE PARK BROCHURE CONTRADICTS THAT, saying year-round camping is available; see the open conflict, and treat the closure as live until it is settled, because acting on 'year-round' costs the trip rather than an argument. 75 campsites: 53 drive-up tent, 10 hike-in tent (#13-22) and 12 RV with full hookups (30 amp), plus Puma Point, a developed group site inside the campground with its own row -- the page's own list sums to 76 while calling itself 75. THE HIKE-IN SITES ARE NOT BACKPACK SITES: they sit inside the campground 0.2 miles (about 1,000 feet) from parking with no vehicle access, EBRPD suggests bringing a wagon, and they are priced at the $25 tent-only rate. NO RIGS OVER 35 FEET, stated twice by the booking system and matching the brochure; the campground page's 'pads average 30 feet, largest is 39' describes pad length, not what may be parked on it. 2 VEHICLES PER CAMPSITE, and the booking system says NO OVERFLOW PARKING IS AVAILABLE while the brochure prices limited overflow parking at $8/night/vehicle -- a second open conflict, and the one that decides where a third car goes. Maximum 8 people per family site, infants and children included. A maximum of TWO family campsites per household, customer name, primary occupant or registered vehicle on any date; additional sites are cancelled. Hot showers, flush toilets, amphitheatre, seasonal campfire programs and a dump station (additional use fees may apply). Every site has a picnic table and fire ring with grill. Tents must stand on dirt or designated pads, never on lawns; there is no limit on the number. FIRES only in designated areas, only commercially bought wood, processed logs or cut lumber -- COLLECTING WOOD IS PROHIBITED, unlike on the national forest land elsewhere in this dataset -- attended by an adult and fully extinguished on departure. Generators, smoking and vaping are prohibited outright. No camp store. LIMITED TO NO CELL SERVICE and no wifi. Beer and wine only, 21+, at campsites or picnic areas and not in parking lots, on trails or at swim beaches; no hard alcohol. PETS: Ordinance 38 s.801.2(i) governs cats and other animals -- attended, and leashed or contained. The campground's own rules are written for dogs: maximum 3 per site, leashed in developed areas, waste binned, CONFINED TO VEHICLE OR TENT DURING QUIET HOURS, never left unattended, and noisy or uncontrollable dogs asked to leave. Whether the quiet-hours confinement is applied to a cat is not stated by any source read here. Sits about 1.5 miles above Lake Chabot; registered campers park free at the Lake Chabot Marina, and swimming is never permitted there. Campsites are for overnight use only -- meet visitors in the day-use parts of the park. EBRPD gives the park as 3,304 acres on its own page and 5,067 on the booking system, and the drive from downtown Oakland as both 20 and 35 minutes; neither gates a decision, so no conflict was opened for them.

name: Dumbarton Quarry Campground on the Bay
coord_source: ReserveAmerica's own overview page for Dumbarton Quarry Campground on the Bay, facility EB/110750 -- a SEPARATE FACILITY from Coyote Hills' EB/110453, which is itself evidence on the park-count thread. Address 9400 Quarry Road, Fremont, reached from I-880 via CA-84 to Paseo Padre North, left on Quarry Road. notes: PARK FIELD RESOLVED TO COYOTE HILLS, where it previously pointed at this campground's own name as a placeholder. Two sources place it inside: ReserveAmerica says it is located within Coyote Hills Regional Park, and Coyote Hills' own map brochure lists it under that park's Camping heading alongside Dairy Glen -- 'Dumbarton Quarry Campground on the Bay offers tent, car, and RV camping'. EBRPD's park finder lists it as a park in its own right, but a finder entry is a navigation choice rather than a claim about boundaries. CAUTION THAT THE JOIN NOW CARRIES: with park set to Coyote Hills, this row inherits Coyote Hills' $5 parking and its six seasonal gate bands, and this campground has its OWN entrance on the Bay side and its own separate brochure. Whether a Dumbarton camper meets Coyote Hills' gate and fee is UNCONFIRMED -- the same shape as Star Mine, which lies in Black Diamond and is entered from Contra Loma. Everything below is still from web-search summaries rather than a page read here. Reported composition, unconfirmed: about 60 paved sites with water, sewer and 50 amp electrical hookups, taking tent, walk-in, bike and RV camping. Open year-round. EVIDENCE AGAINST THE RESOLUTION, ARRIVING THE SAME DAY: ReserveAmerica's Coyote Hills listing says 'Dumbarton Quarry and Ardenwood Historic Farm parks are located nearby' -- calling Dumbarton a PARK, and placing it NEARBY rather than inside. That is the third source and it lines up with EBRPD's park finder, not with the brochure. The resolution is left standing, because a brochure listing a campground under a park's own Camping heading is a stronger claim about boundaries than a sentence pointing visitors at what else is in the area, and 'nearby' is what you would write about a camp with its own entrance a few miles round the marsh even if it sat inside the same park. But the reading is now 2-2 across sources rather than 2-1, and the caution above about inheriting Coyote Hills' gate and fee matters more for it. THE BALANCE SHIFTED AGAIN ON 2026-09-16, AND THE RESOLUTION IS KEPT ANYWAY. Dumbarton has its OWN ReserveAmerica facility page, EB/110750, separate from Coyote Hills' EB/110453 -- so the booking system that was cited as placing it 'within Coyote Hills Regional Park' also sells it as a facility in its own right, and on Coyote Hills' page calls it a park located nearby. Against the Coyote Hills brochure listing it under that park's Camping heading, the count is now roughly three to one AGAINST. It is kept because a brochure's Camping heading is still the only source making a claim about BOUNDARIES, while a separate booking facility and a park-finder entry are claims about how EBRPD organises its own systems -- Star Mine has a separate entrance too and nobody doubts it is in Black Diamond. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is Dumbarton's own page on ebparks.org, which has not been read. ONE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS NOW GONE: this row has its own coordinate, at campground precision, off its own facility page, so no search depends on the park field to place it. What still depends on it is the $5 parking and the six seasonal gate bands it inherits from Coyote Hills, and this camp has its own entrance at 9400 Quarry Road, about two miles from Coyote Hills' own point.

THE WALK IS 3.4 OR 3.6 MILES depending which source you read: the booking system gives 18,000 feet, which is 3.41 miles, and the park page says 3.6 from the Marsh Creek Staging Area. Neither gates a decision at that margin, so no conflict thread was opened, but a party carrying every litre of its own water should plan for the longer one. SUMMER HEAT IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT: EBRPD warns temperatures here commonly exceed 100F, and this is a multi-mile carry to a site with no water. 2 vehicles. Parking passes are emailed about a week before and MUST BE PRINTED and displayed on the dash. Haul out all trash. NO DOGS ANYWHERE IN THIS PARK -- see the park-scoped rule; the reason is the endangered San Joaquin kit fox, to which dogs are a disease vector. Pets allowed here are listed as HORSE only. Round Valley is open year round, despite the booking system labelling the loop 'Backpack Seasonal'.

name: Dairy Glen Group Camp
coord_source: ReserveAmerica's Coyote Hills Regional Park overview page, read 2026-09-16. PARK PRECISION, NOT THE CAMP'S: the pair is published on the park overview, not on Dairy Glen's own campsite page, which gives none. Coyote Hills is 1,266 acres by the park page and 978 by this same listing, so the camp may be a mile or more from this point. Good enough to answer 'how far is this from Oakland'; not good enough to navigate to.
nightly_entry_cutoff: Park gate hours run in six seasonal bands and the park has a separate CURFEW of 10pm-5am -- see the park's access row.
notes: ACCESS IS HIKE-IN, WHICH CORRECTS THIS PROJECT'S OWN DRIVE-IN TAG -- the second such correction in two days, after Star Mine, and worse than that one because nothing supported the original. Star Mine's drive_in came from a page saying parking was available at the site; Dairy Glen's came from nowhere. No source read yesterday said how you reach it, and drive_in was written anyway because a group camp with three shade structures and a 6ft stone BBQ sounded like somewhere you park. THE BOOKING SYSTEM SAYS THE OPPOSITE, TWICE: 'This is a HIKE-IN only site (approximately 1/4 mile on a flat, paved surface)' and 'Dairy Glen Group Site is open year-round. Hike-in ONLY site. NO vehicle access (driving into/out of site).' So a party of up to fifty carries its kit a quarter mile, and the ten vehicles the listing permits stay at the lot. The quarter mile is FLAT AND PAVED, which is why the ADA claim below survives the correction rather than being undone by it. MINIMUM 17, MAXIMUM 50 -- and the minimum was recorded here yesterday as NOT STATED ON ANY PAGE READ, with a derivation from the District's 2026 tier table guessing 17 and a warning that the table's row alignment had been reconstructed and found wrong in one place. The derivation was right. That is one confirmed hit, not a licence to trust the table: the row that was wrong is still wrong. MAXIMUM 10 VEHICLES. Check-in 2:00 PM, check-out 12:00 PM. A SECURITY DEPOSIT is required, as at Star Mine. Open year-round. PETS ALLOWED: DOMESTIC, stated on the listing -- which matters against Star Mine, where the same field is simply absent and the contrast was flagged as worth asking Reservations about. Two group camps in one district, one marked and one not, is now a pattern rather than a one-off omission. FACILITIES, fuller than the park page gave: three shade structures, three 20ft picnic tables, a 6ft stone BBQ, a drinking fountain, a FIRE CIRCLE WITH BENCHES, a hand-washing station and vault toilets. The listing marks Campfire Allowed, Fire Pit, BBQ and Lean To/Shelter, and marks the site ADA ACCESSIBLE. FULLY ADA COMPLIANT after a Regional Parks Foundation renovation, with a hardened path to the shade structures for wheelchairs and mobility devices -- still the only campground in this project described as accessible rather than merely having an accessible toilet, and the booking system's own ADA flag now agrees with the park page. THE FIRE PIT AGAINST THE REST OF THIS DATASET: EBRPD's backpack sites ban fires outright and Black Diamond bans them park-wide, so a provided pit and a lit fire circle are the exception, and Ordinance 38 s.404's 'only in the facilities provided' is what governs it. BOOKING DEADLINE IS THIS PARK'S OWN, NOT THE DISTRICT'S -- see the coyote-hills-group booking channel: paid in full five working days ahead, or three days if you are collecting parking passes or permits. Yesterday's note here said '3 or more business days', which is the District figure and is not what this camp asks.

name: Arroyo Flats Group Camp
coord_source: ReserveAmerica's Garin Regional Park overview page, read 2026-09-16. PARK PRECISION. The same page gives Arroyo Flats' street address as 1320 Garin Avenue while the park page says 1580, so even the addresses on this park disagree; a park centroid is the most this project can honestly claim.
nightly_entry_cutoff: Garin's gate closes between 6pm and 9pm depending on the season, and the site's own instructions are to check those hours and enter before closing -- see the park's access row, including the two days in October that fall in no published band.
fee_notes: NO NIGHTLY RATE ON FILE -- absent is not free, and the site fee must be confirmed with EBRPD Reservations. A SEPARATE COST IS STATED AND IS NOT THAT FEE: beer and wine at a group campsite require an additional permit costing $25.00, purchased in advance by phone. A SECURITY DEPOSIT is also required, amount not stated. This is the first dollar figure this project has for the District's group alcohol permit, recorded only as 'a separate permit' since Briones. NOTE WHAT THE COST HEADER ABOVE CANNOT SAY: the $25 makes this component report as charging, which is true and is not the same as knowing what a night here costs. Same shape as the cpma permit, whose fee is free for the permit and $5.00 per day for the parking.
notes: ACCESS IS HIKE-IN, recorded as such from the first reading rather than corrected into it. 'It is a .25 mile hike-in to the site from parking.' That makes three of three: Star Mine, Dairy Glen and now Arroyo Flats are all quarter-mile hike-ins, which is why Briones' three camps carrying drive_in on a single unsourced answer is worth re-asking rather than assuming. MINIMUM PARTY SIZE IS CONTRADICTED BY EBRPD'S OWN TWO PAGES -- see the arroyo-flats-minimum thread. The booking system's site details say Minimum Number of People 17 and its own site note repeats 'CAPACITY: minimum 17, maximum 75'. The park page says the site 'can accommodate groups of 25 people or more, up to 75'. A party of twenty is booked by one page and refused by the other, and group sites are booked BY PHONE, so the figure Reservations applies is the one that decides it. The 25 matches the District's capacity tier table, corrected at Briones to 300/100, 100/50, 75/25, 50/17, 35/17 -- so two sources say 25 and the booking system says 17. Maximum 75 is agreed. PARKING AND THE LOCKED GATE: 15 parking passes and NO overflow. TWO vehicles may park at the site, conditions permitting; the other thirteen park in the lot. NO SHUTTLING BACK AND FORTH, as at Star Mine. There is a LOCKED GATE for the group site; a combination code and an information letter are emailed 5-10 days before arrival -- and the same park's overview page says that letter comes 5-7 days before. Recorded as published: the two figures differ by three days, and a party that has not had the code cannot get in. FACILITIES, primitive: five 10ft picnic tables, one DOUBLE BBQ, a drinking fountain, one FIRE CIRCLE WITH BENCHES and two CHEMICAL TOILETS. NO FLUSH TOILETS AND NO SHOWERS, stated outright. The listing marks BBQ, Campfire Allowed, Fire Pit, Picnic Table, Privacy and Security Deposit, shade or tree cover PARTIAL, and Pets Allowed: Domestic. Open year round. THE FIRE CIRCLE against the rest of this dataset: EBRPD's backpack sites ban fires outright and Black Diamond bans them park-wide, so Arroyo Flats joins Dairy Glen as an exception, and the District's firewood rule applies -- commercially purchased wood, processed logs or cut lumber only, and collecting wood is prohibited.
